CHIEF COMPLAINT
Annual exam

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Evelyn is a 56-year-old female with a past medical history significant for coronary artery disease with prior stenting, prior carpal tunnel release, and herniated disc who presents for her annual exam.

Regarding her herniated disc, the patient reports that it has been doing well since steroid injection several months ago. She denies back pain or limitations in movement.

Regarding her carpal tunnel, the patient states that she had surgery a couple of years ago and has had no recurrent issues. She is back to work with full range of motion and denies numbing and tingling in her hands.

Regarding her coronary artery disease, the patient reports having chest pain over the last month. The chest pain occurs when she walks and resolves with rest. She denies chest pain at rest. She describes the pain as burning in quality and denies associated shortness of breath, nausea, or vomiting. She rates the pain as not concerning enough to warrant an ER visit. The pain is located in the middle of her chest and occurs approximately three times per week.

The patient also reports nasal congestion from allergies related to pollen.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Positive for chest pain and nasal congestion from allergies. Negative for shortness of breath, nausea, vomiting, lower extremity edema, muscle aches, fever, or chills.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
1. Coronary artery disease with prior stenting
2. Prior carpal tunnel release
3. Herniated disc with prior steroid injection

MEDICATIONS
Continue aspirin and Toprol. Starting Crestor 20 mg once daily.

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient is back to work.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital signs: Blood pressure well controlled, oxygenation normal.
Cardiac: Slight 3/6 systolic ejection murmur.
Pulmonary: Lungs clear to auscultation.
Vascular: No carotid bruits.
Extremities: No lower extremity edema. Healed surgical scars on right wrist.

RESULTS
Echocardiogram from last year: Left ventricular ejection fraction 45%, slight mitral regurgitation.
ECG: Stable, reflects prior coronary artery disease with no new changes.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Carpal tunnel release: Patient doing well. No further intervention needed at this time. Patient advised to report if recurring symptoms develop.
2. Herniated disc: Patient doing well. No further steroid injection or physical therapy needed at this time. Patient advised to report if recurrent symptoms develop.
3. Coronary artery disease with chest pain: Most concerning problem. Continue aspirin and Toprol. Order cardiac stress test to evaluate for additional blockages. Order lipid panel. Start Crestor 20 mg once daily.
